candidates.title: Longitudinal panel of stove adoption
candidates.text: Follow households for five years after a programme and record continued use. The panel design separates early enthusiasm from sustained change.

candidates.title: Randomised reminder trial
candidates.text: Send usage reminders to half of a sample and compare sustained adoption. It isolates habit formation from the cost of the stove itself.

candidates.title: Price sensitivity study
candidates.text: Vary fuel price within a region and measure switching back to biomass. It gives the elasticity a subsidy would have to overcome.

candidates.title: Supply reliability study
candidates.text: Measure adoption where refill supply is intermittent against where it is steady. Supply, not preference, may be what decides continued use.

candidates.title: Qualitative cooking-practice study
candidates.text: Interview cooks about which meals they still cook on the old stove, and why. It explains partial adoption that survey counts miss.

candidates.title: Health endpoint linkage
candidates.text: Link adoption records to clinic visits for respiratory illness over three years. It connects the intervention to the outcome people care about.

candidates.title: Time-use substitution study
candidates.text: Measure whether time saved on fuel collection is reallocated, and to what. It tests the economic case rather than the health one.

candidates.title: Second-hand market survey
candidates.text: Survey resale of distributed stoves as an indicator of abandonment. Resale is a signal that no self-report will give you.
